name: ame
description: The Ame resolver. Sets name the four token layers; modifiers name the axes a recipe varies on, one modifier per axis, its contexts the values that axis takes. This is the DTCG Resolver module doing what it was written for: alternate values per context, deduplicated, with the permutations enumerable rather than written out. What it deliberately does NOT yet carry is the theme axis: light and dark are still the -on-dark token pairs the alias map re-points under [data-theme=dark] (contract B3), which predates this document. That is the next axis to move here, and it is named rather than left implied by a document that looks like it covers theming and does not.

semantic.description: Decisions, each a reference to a base primitive.

recipe.description: Per-slot values for one component, in its default resolution.

org.metis.recipe.$description: The structure of each recipe: which element it dresses, the class its root carries, and its slots. It lives here rather than in the token files because the DTCG format has no notion of a slot, and $extensions on a set is where the spec puts vendor data. `static` holds the declarations no DTOS type expresses — a keyword, a percentage, a function over tokens — the same disclosure contract.md > Spec gaps already makes for em, vh and the dither asset. Every var() inside a static names a real token, and RC1 checks it, so a static cannot drift from the token layer either.

root.description: The card itself: the bordered surface both callers share.

list.description: The definition list, laid out as the column grid.

cell.description: One column. min-width 0 lets it shrink to its grid track; a grid item defaults to min-width:auto and would refuse to shrink below its content, which is where the overflow came from.

block.description: The label-and-values block inside a cell. display:contents by default, so on the home the wrapper is not in the layout at all; the term sheet gives it a box to centre.

label.description: The dt. margin-top 0 drops the prose `dt { margin-top: 1.25em }` it inherits inside DocsBody.

value.description: The dd. padding-inline-start 0 drops the prose `dd { padding-inline-start: 1.625em }`; overflow-wrap breaks a long unbroken value inside its column rather than through its neighbour.

theme.description: Light or dark. The system-wide axis: it re-points tokens rather than any one component's slots, so it carries no recipe and compiles to a document-wide scope instead of a class.

org.metis.theme.$description:
Dark used to be six hand-listed alias pairs in build.mjs plus an -on-dark naming convention, which meant a third theme needed new suffixed tokens and a new convention rather than a file. It is a context now: theme/dark.json overrides the tokens it disagrees with, and a high-contrast theme is another context beside it.

`document` is what makes it reach further than a class scope. The attribute sits on a wrapper deep in the page, but html, body and any body-level portal are ABOVE that wrapper and inherit nothing from it — which is why the page ground and the scrollbar were hand-mirrored literals for so long. Emitting the scope for the document element as well, selected with :has(), gives them the same values every other element gets.

expertise-card.layout.description: Which of the two callers the expertise card is dressing. The default context is the portfolio home; the term sheet is a case study's scope facts.

org.metis.recipe.$description: An attribute axis: the context is selected on the element, so it compiles to an attribute selector on the recipe's root and is settable per instance.

expertise-card.viewport.description: How wide the viewport is. The contexts are the resolver's own sizing example (small, medium, large) applied to one recipe's track count and padding.

org.metis.recipe.$description: A media axis: the context is selected by the viewport, not by the markup, so it compiles to @media (min-width: <token>) and takes no attribute. The resolver picks exactly one context per resolution; min-width queries stack, so the widest matching context wins — the same selection, reached by the cascade instead of by the tool. Each context names the breakpoint TOKEN, never a literal width.
